answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with dual-domain identity binding: before an identity earns full rights, it must link two independent, costly histories — a long-lived code-signing key with a public merged-work record, and a payment channel with settled trades. Like a jetty held by both pilings, or an orchard checked each season, the binding is verified on-ledger; a mismatch in either domain voids the identity at its zenith and burns its bond. Forging a fake then means fabricating two unrelated histories, so attack cost doubles while honest agents pay nothing new.
